content.text: InstagramLog InSign UpCloseNever miss a post from andalusilearnSign up for Instagram to stay in the loop.Sign upLog inAudio is mutedandalusilearn•FollowOriginal audioMore optionsandalusilearn 41wWhat does “Eid Mubarak” mean⁉️☪️🥳Breakdown:Phrase: “عِيد مُبَارَك” (Eid Mubarak)Transliteration: Eid MubarakMeaning: “Blessed Festival”This phrase is made up of two words:‎ 1. “عِيد” (Eid) – which means “festival” or “celebration” in English. It refers specifically to the Islamic festivals of Eid al-Fitr (at the end of Ramadan) and Eid al-Adha (after Hajj).‎ 2. “مُبَارَك” (Mubarak) – which means “blessed” or “congratulations” in English. It is a way of offering good wishes.🔑Keywords:‎ 1. عِيد: Eid – Festival/Celebration‎ 2. مُبَارَك: Mubarak – BlessedThe phrase “Eid Mubarak” is commonly used by Muslims around the world to greet each other during the celebrations of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.Learn Arabic Sentence by Sentence Ep.136 📝Load more commentswalewicki 41wLikeReplymr_nisaar_05 41wEid ul adha Mubarak ❤️🙌LikeReplyView all 1 repliesLike34Comment3ShareSaveJune 6, 2025Log in to like or comment.More posts from andalusilearnClipClipClipClipClipClipClipClipClipSee more posts
